title: Conscious Immortality
subtitle: Paul Brunton's notebook of conversations with Sri Ramana Maharshi, recorded in the 1930s.
meta_description: Conscious Immortality — Paul Brunton and Munagala Venkataramaiah's record of conversations with Sri Ramana Maharshi in the 1930s. Free to read and download.
body_html:
About the Book

Conscious Immortality is one of the most intimate records of Bhagavan Sri Ramana Maharshi ever set down. It is a notebook of conversations compiled from the journals of Paul Brunton and Munagala S. Venkataramaiah (who also compiled the celebrated Talks with Sri Ramana Maharshi) during the second half of the 1930s. The book was first published by Sri Ramanasramam in 1984 and has since gone through several revised editions.

Brunton's role in this record is unique. When he met Bhagavan in 1931 and described the encounter in A Search in Secret India, he introduced Ramana Maharshi to the English-speaking world. In the years that followed, Brunton returned and kept a private notebook of questions and answers, notes he never intended for publication. After Brunton's death, his son Kenneth Hurst gifted these notebooks to the Ashram, and they form the core of Conscious Immortality.

"The Maharshi's method is to turn the mind back upon itself. He does not teach philosophic doctrines nor discuss religious dogmas. He simply teaches one to know oneself — to discover the Self."
Paul Brunton

What the Book Contains

The conversations range across every dimension of the inner life: the nature of the Self and its realisation, the practice of self-enquiry, the role of the guru, the meaning of death and rebirth, the states of sleep and deep samadhi, the relationship between effort and grace, and the silence that underlies all teaching. Bhagavan answers Brunton's sometimes probing, sometimes sceptical questions with the characteristic directness and economy that mark all his recorded exchanges.

About half the material in Conscious Immortality also appears in Talks with Sri Ramana Maharshi, but the overlap is not mere repetition; the contexts differ and the emphases illuminate each other in valuable ways. The remainder is found nowhere else.

Bhagavan on Paul Brunton

Ramana Maharshi himself acknowledged Brunton's role as his medium to the West. When asked about Brunton, Bhagavan said Brunton had been sent to him and that through him the teaching would spread. This endorsement, coming from the Maharshi, is of the highest order, and it is why Brunton's written record carries a special weight among the primary sources.

A Book to Keep Close

This is not a book to read once and set aside. Devotees who have spent years with Conscious Immortality report that passages which seemed clear on first reading open to entirely new depths with the passage of time and the deepening of practice. It is particularly valued by those drawn to the direct path, the Short Path, because Brunton's questions come from someone who has studied comparative philosophy and approaches Bhagavan from genuine intellectual rigour, drawing out answers that address the seeker at every level.
